sentences.text: Ms. Mansi Kushwah - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Amit Raval Ga for the State.
 Shri Aman Mourya- Advocate for the respondent [Comp].

Order 
1. This first application has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No. 184 of 2024 registered at Police Station- Mandleshwar, District - Khargone (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(n), 376(3) of the IPC and section 5(L)/6 and 3/4(2) of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 22/07/2024.
2. Learned Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in this matter under the pressure of family members of the victim.
The victim had left her parental home at her own will and came to live with the applicant.
They stayed together for almost two NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9531 2 MCRC-2587-2025 months at Surat (Gujrat).
Learned counsel referring to the evidence of victim (PW-1) submits that the victim did not support the prosecution and exonerated the applicant of the alleged offence.
She has stated that due to ill-treatment of her parents, she left her parental home and the applicant did not commit any misconduct with her.
There is no likelihood of tampering with the remaining evidence by the applicant.
The fate of prosecution against the applicant is apparent.
The applicant is aged around 22 years.
He is a labourer by profession.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per Contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State ably assisted by learned counsel for the objector oppose the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence and submits that the applicant had kidnapped the victim on earlier occasion also.
The victim was aged around 15 years and 7 months at the time of the incident.
She was unable to understand the consequence of her act and conduct, therefore, the applicant may not be extended the benefit of bail..
However, after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
4 . Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application and the case diary.

5. Allegedly, the applicant kidnapped the minor victim and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9531 3 MCRC-2587-2025 subjected her to sexual assault, however, the victim did not support the prosecution and exonerated the applicant of the alleged offence in her evidence recorded before the trial Court.
The veracity of the prosecution will be considered after evidence in trial.
As informed, the applicant is aged around 22 years and is a labourer by profession.
He has family to look after.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of criminal antecedents, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant,
there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with remaining evidence or influencing the remaining witnesses by the applicant or repeating the offence.
The trial would take time to conclude.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.
However, the observations, herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

6. Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforesaid facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, present application is allowed.

7. Accordingly, it is directed that applicant-Raja s hall be released on bail in connection with the crime as stated in para-1 of this order, upon furnishing personal bond and surety bond of amount, as may be considered appropriate by the Trial Court/Committal Court for compliance with conditions,
as may be imposed by such Court under NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9531 4 MCRC-2587-2025 Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C. 1973/ Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023, to secure presence of the applicant for the trial.
8. This order shall be effective till the end of trial.
However, in case of breach of any of the preconditions of bail, the Trial Court may consider, on merit, cancellation of bail without any impediment of this order.
9. The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
C.C. as per rules.

(SANJEEV S KALGAONKAR) JUDGE amol Raja vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18508858/
